headline: A firm answer to the Marquis
summary: Roosevelt replies to De Mores that he is no enemy, but that he will not be cowed by any threat and stands ready to answer for anything he has said or done.

events.detail: Writes De Mores denying hostility while refusing to be intimidated

tr_quotes.text: Most emphatically I am not your enemy; if I were you would know it, for I would be an open one, and would not have asked you to my house nor gone to yours. As your final words, however, seem to imply a threat it is due to myself to say that the statement is not made through any fear of possible consequences to me; I too, as you know, am always on hand, and ever ready to hold myself accountable in any way for anything I have said or done. Yours very truly, Theodore Roosevelt

headline: A party private; Edith again
summary: Roosevelt joins the crowd at the Republican State Committee meeting in New York City and tells a Tribune reporter he is ready for orders. The house is now renamed Sagamore Hill for the Sagamore Mohannis, who signed the land away two centuries before.
